title: Surjectivity of the canonical saturation generator on its return sheet
statement: For finite fields k₁/k₀ with #k₁=(#k₀)^r, let c:C→X be a monomorphism compatible with the structural maps, and let the open immersion v:Cbar→Xbar satisfy both specified projection equations and Fr_C;v=v;Fr_X^r. For any all-proetale Weil sheaves V on X and G on C and any Weil morphism i:G→P_all(V), the explicitly defined saturationUnit of [def-zl-frobenius-saturation], applied to the carrier of i and the comparison of [def-zl-powered-pullback-carrier], is an epimorphism. No lissity, constructibility, smoothness, finite type, or monicity of i is assumed. This is a property of a fixed constructed map and asserts no existence of a lifted subobject.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: For every nonreturn integer n, the restricted free summand is zero, by the disjoint-sheet vanishing theorem. Its map therefore factors through the original carrier map via zero.
For n=rm, use the return-translate factorization theorem, proved by the free-algebra shift recursion and equivariance of the powered pullback.

The pullback preserves the integer coproduct and the image quotient. For each summand, cancel the restricted image inclusion against its factorization through the original map to factor the corresponding map to the restricted saturation through saturationUnit. If two maps agree after saturationUnit, they agree after every restricted coprojection, hence after the pulled-back image quotient. That quotient is epi, so the maps agree and saturationUnit is epi.

proof_origin.note: A5: avoid constructing the full tensor splitting. Disjointness follows by epi cancellation on a nonempty sheet intersection and the finite-field Frobenius order; combine with the integer shift factorization and the explicit image quotient.
